A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IRIS benchmark and baseline framework. All 29 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, figures, and tables, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: v1 reports original parameter-estimation, equation-classification, extrapolation, identifiability, and ablation results on IRIS and Delfys75, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds coupling-validation and multi-clip training comparisons in Tables 14 and 15.

M1.justification: The new multi-clip variant trains one shared encoder–physics model across training clips and applies it to held-out clips, supplementing independent per-clip fitting (v3 Section 6.4 and Appendix I). This is a limited procedural adaptation; the existing architecture, ODE bank, corrected integrator, rollout loss, and routing methods remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The datasets and eight IRIS phenomena remain. Reported hitting-cone coverage expands from one default condition in v1 Table S1 to slow, mid, and fast conditions in v3 Table 9, with evaluations in Table 14. Because v1 already lists 240 videos for equation routing, the PDFs do not establish that all 20 additional inventoried videos were newly collected.

E2.justification: v3 adds a no-coupling control for hitting cones and reports a frozen-VLM-plus-classifier-head development trial alongside LoRA. The RK4 comparison disappears with v1 Appendix L, although the Störmer-Verlet summary remains. The principal CNN, VLM, and original/corrected Euler comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a substantially different evaluation design: an 80/20 split by sorted clip index, shared-model training, and evaluation against per-clip fitting on the same held-out clips. It also adds controlled coupling evaluation using reconstruction MSE. These supplement the retained train-per-clip protocol; newly disclosed CNN settings alone do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds coupling ablation, cross-clip transfer analysis, parameter trajectories, and additional prompting diagnostics. Conversely, v1's pendulum period-correction analysis and detailed horizon and integrator comparisons disappear (Appendices J–L, Tables S7–S9). Qualitative horizon and Störmer-Verlet findings remain in the main text, but their detailed supporting analyses are removed.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies triplicate geometric measurements, ten independent damping fits, and a coefficient-of-variation summary for learned coupling. These expand statistical documentation without establishing additional model runs. Seed 42, the ten-recording trial design, and the retained mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 14 reports coupling-related MSE reductions of 6.0%, 19.0%, and 10.5%. New Table 15 reports per-clip versus multi-clip MAE, including 0.207 versus 0.046 for dropping-ball gravity and 0.507 versus 22.06 for pendulum length. These are new-protocol results, not improvements over matched v1 runs. Tables 4–8 and v1 Table S5/v3 Table 13 retain their numerical results, while Tables S7–S9 are removed.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1 Appendix J's exact pendulum-period expression using the complete elliptic integral, the relative period-correction definition, and associated mathematical analysis. The principal ODEs, loss equations, calibration mappings, and Euler-Cromer update remain; expanded explanations do not constitute new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion change the benchmark-size claim from 220 to 240 videos. The contribution list also recasts the multi-step baseline as a training objective for equation identification with stability analysis. The central benchmark, five-axis protocol, routing comparison, and multi-body instability claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations that learned coupling captures physical interaction and shared training reveals transferable physical inductive bias, with a shared-latent-space explanation for pendulum failure. It newly states that explicit pixel-to-metre calibration and propagation of tracking-noise uncertainty are absent, and qualifies identifiability analysis as preliminary. The earlier warning about incomplete segmentation-mask availability disappears. These materially expand the paper's interpretations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: CNN pretraining, frame resolution and validation split; a VLM prompt and access provider; ground-truth tracking and fitting procedures; encoder weight sharing; and CSV fields and processing scripts. These are mostly disclosures, not demonstrated implementation changes. Conversely, the explicit 7/1/2 split description and direct dataset link disappear, while the project address changes.

R1.justification: The distinct cited works and related-work coverage are essentially unchanged; v3's additional Schmidt–Lipson entry duplicates an already cited work. However, Section 7 newly claims that 240 videos exceeds all prior real-world benchmarks, strengthening the comparative positioning despite Table 3 listing VideoPhy with 688 videos.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes and expands the narrative: contributions are rewritten, related-work subsections become run-in headings, the real-data motivation subsection is removed, and open challenges and limitations are merged. Existing appendix explanations are extensively expanded, while the final three analytical appendices are replaced by a different supplementary organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and expanded from seven displayed phenomenon columns to eight. v3 adds two experimental tables, removes Tables S7–S9, and relocates several retained appendix tables to the final pages. Expanded takeaway captions, revised table coloring, and a larger page format with wider margins produce substantial presentation changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new coupling and held-out multi-clip comparisons address empirical questions absent from v1, and expanded implementation details aid reproducibility. However, v3 removes detailed horizon and integrator evidence while retaining their claims. It also newly says the IRIS one-step gravity advantage mirrors Delfys75, although Table 5 shows the opposite trend. These gains in breadth and transparency coexist with weakened support and new interpretive inconsistencies, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
